answer:
Both halves of the curator's alternative are legitimate in CRM terms, but they are not symmetric, and the two things being asked about behave very differently. Documenting the sequencing and pointing at the accession is squarely inside the model. Holding the nucleotide string locally is permitted, but it is a preservation decision rather than a modelling one. The bootstrap-support values are the part the CRM does not represent, and I would not stretch it to cover them.

1. WHAT THE COLLECTION DATABASE SHOULD DEFINITELY HOLD

The specimen is an E20 Biological Object. The sequencing run is an S4 Single Observation (CRMsci): S27 Observation's scope note is explicit that the output of the internal processes of measurement devices is regarded as part of the observation and not as additional inference, and that primary data from such devices are results of observation, so the sequencer's read is the observation's result rather than a separate interpretation. Record it as P14 carried out by the genomics lab, P4 has time-span, P177 assigned property of type pointing at a term such as "mitochondrial DNA sequence" (S4 quantifies P177 as necessary), P140 assigned attribute to the specimen, and O16 observed value pointing at the sequence.

The sequence itself is a D9 Data Object (CRMdig) - its scope note covers exactly digital objects that are the result of measurements or other observations and/or their algorithmic evaluation in the form of structured data. D9 quantifies P70 documents as necessary, which forces the link back to the specimen; that is the join the curator actually needs, and it is why D9 is preferable here to a bare E73.

The accession number is an E42 Identifier of that data object, attached with P1 is identified by and typed with P2 has type. Because the number was issued by the public database and not by you, record the issuing act as E15 Identifier Assignment: P37 assigned the E42, P14 carried out by the database's operator, P140 assigned attribute to the D9. connect confirms that P1 is a declared shortcut for precisely that path through E15 and P37, so using E15 is the fully developed form of the pointer, not an extra layer.

2. THE NUCLEOTIDE STRING: EITHER IS CORRECT, AND THE CRM SAYS WHICH TO PREFER

The model gives you both options and they are siblings by design. P190 has symbolic content holds the content inside the knowledge base - a "complete, identifying representation of its content in the form of an instance of E62 String". P200 has complete copy (domain E90 Symbolic Object, range E25 Human-Made Feature) is the same idea pointing outward at the copy sitting on the public database's server; like P190 it "only applies to instances of E90 Symbolic Object that can completely be represented by discrete symbols", which a nucleotide sequence is.

That pair is the outcome of SIG issue 490, "How to model a file" (Done). Martin Doerr laid out the two forms there and attached a condition to the outward one: "the maintainers of the archive must guarantee that the identifier will be uniquely connected with the content", otherwise a URL in a knowledge base is inadequate. A public sequence database's accession number does carry that guarantee, so the pointer is sufficient. Duplicating the string locally adds no new fact in CRM terms - only a second representation of the same E90 - so do it only if you want independence from that repository, and then treat it as a copy, not as a new assertion.

The decision criterion is in the specification itself: "only concepts to be used for selecting multiple instances from the knowledge base by formal querying need to be explicitly modelled". You will not query your collection across specimens by nucleotide string, so the string is content, not structure.

3. THE TREE STATISTICS: THIS IS WHERE TO STOP

Bootstrap support is a per-node resampling statistic belonging to one analysis run. There is no CRM class or property for it, and every near miss fails for a reason. E16 Measurement is out: since 7.1.1 it pertains only to E18 Physical Thing and yields an E54 Dimension, and the specification's own migration note says that dimensions of conceptual objects "may be inferred by other forms of E13 Attribute Assignment" such as data evaluation - a support value is a number about a hypothesised clade, not a measured property of the fish. D11 Digital Measurement Event plus L61 contains value set of would let a data object carry the value set of an E54 Dimension, but a support proportion is not a dimension of anything you hold. CRMinf comes closest - I2 Belief with J5 holds to be an I6 Belief Value, whose scope note admits probability and fuzziness, produced by an I5 Inference Making that used the sequence as premise - but an I6 value qualifies one proposition held by one actor, so a whole tree would need one I2 Belief per clade. That is domain modelling inside a collection management system, and the SIG's long-running discussion of attaching qualification to individual statements never resolved it ("E13/P141 lacks precision to address a specific statement"). Note too that CRMsci's own answer for confidence in an observation is a free-text P3 has note, not a statistic.

So keep the tree as an opaque D9 Data Object with its provenance recorded - who ran it, when, on which input sequences, with which method (P32 used general technique or P33 used specific technique) - and store from the analysis the one thing a collection database exists for: the taxonomic determination. E17 Type Assignment is the class, and the SIG fixed that reading for natural history in issue 77, whose background states that the classification procedure or E17 Type assignment would be called Determination for genetically related living beings, and that "It includes both Systematic and Molecular identification", explicitly via gene bank. Use P41 classified for the specimen, P42 assigned for the taxon as an E55 Type, P16 used specific object for the tree data object as the evidence relied on, P14 carried out by for the sequencing team, and P3 has note if you want the support figure legible to a human reader.

4. WHY THIS LINE AND NOT ANOTHER

The division is the SIG's own, from the first natural history requirements discussion. The background to issues 76 and 77 separates natural history documentation into "ordinary collection management issues and the taxonomic discourse", treats the first as already covered by the CRM, and is willing to leave formalisation outside the model where it does not pay - of ecosystem structure it says formalisation "seems however to be beyond the practical scope of the CRM". Per-node phylogenetic statistics sit on that far side. Your collection database should carry the specimen, the sequencing event, the sequence as an identified data object with its accession, the determination that followed, and a provenanced pointer to the tree; the tree's internal numbers stay in the analytical system that produced them.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: Its scope was reduced in 7.1.1 to instances of E18 Physical Thing with an E54 Dimension as result. A base-call sequence has no unit and no numeric value, so P40 observed dimension / P90 has value cannot carry it. The same migration note is what rules E16 out for bootstrap values as well.

rejected_alternatives.option: D11 Digital Measurement Event (for the sequencing run)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Its own scope note routes the machine output through an observed-dimension property to E54 Dimension and then to D9 via L61 contains value set of, i.e. it is built for instrument readings that are quantities with a value set. A nucleotide sequence is a symbol sequence, not a dimension value set. S4 with O16 observed value carries a non-numeric observed value directly.

rejected_alternatives.option: I6 Belief Value with I2 Belief and J5 holds to be (for the bootstrap values)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: This is the nearest structured hook in the family - I6 explicitly allows probability or fuzziness rather than only TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN - and it is the right construct if you want to record a single confidence on the one taxonomic conclusion you assert. It does not scale to a tree: an I6 value qualifies one proposition held by one actor, so per-clade support would require one I2 Belief per node.

rejected_alternatives.option: I5 Inference Making (for the phylogenetic analysis)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Defensible as a way to trace the analysis from premise to conclusion, and it would be correct if the collection database were meant to hold the argumentation. For a collection catalogue it buys nothing the E17 Type Assignment plus a provenanced tree file does not already give, and it invites the per-clade belief explosion above.

rejected_alternatives.option: E54 Dimension reached by L61 contains value set of
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Technically legal from a D9, but it misstates what the number is: P43 has dimension attaches dimensions to an E70 Thing, so the bearer would end up being the tree file rather than the clade the support value is about.

rejected_alternatives.option: E73 Information Object (plain CRMbase, instead of D9)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Acceptable if you refuse the CRMdig extension, and P190 / P200 / P1 all still apply since D9 inherits them. Rejected only because D9's scope note names exactly this kind of object - the structured result of observation and its algorithmic evaluation - and because D9 quantifies P70 documents as necessary, which forces the link back to the specimen that the curator's question is really about.

rejected_alternatives.option: E62 String on the specimen record (a plain sequence column)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P190's domain is E90 Symbolic Object, so the string has to hang off an information object anyway. Storing only a string loses the identity of the sequence as something that can be identified by an accession, dated, attributed to the lab and pointed at from outside.

Strictly the sequencing was performed on a tissue subsample, not the whole fish, and S13 with a sample-taking event is the right refinement if the lab retains and curates that extract. Left out because the question does not turn on the subsample and adding it would not change the storage decision.

siblings_considered.why_not: E22 Human-Made Object is the other subclass of E19 Physical Object, and it requires the object to have been purposely created by human activity. A fish caught in a river survey is a natural biological item; only its preparation and mounting are human work, and that is modelled as events on the E20, not by reclassifying it.

S21 Measurement is the other main subclass of S27 Observation, and it is for properties determined as quantities by a systematic procedure, which is why E16 Measurement sits under it. The result here is a symbol sequence with no unit, and S21 offers no property that can carry a non-numeric observed value, whereas S4 has O16 observed value with range E1.

D35 Area is the other surviving subclass of D1 Digital Object and denotes a portion or region of interest inside a media object. The deposited sequence and the tree are whole structured datasets, not areas within one. Honestly, no sibling of D9 is a real rival here - the genuine competition came from its own parents D1 and E31, which I weighed separately.

E35 Title is the other subclass of E41 Appellation that could carry a short string, but it covers strings identifiable as titles within a cultural context. An accession number is a code allocated by a registry to guarantee unique reference, which is precisely E42's scope.

E16 Measurement is a sibling under E13 Attribute Assignment, but the public database's act allocates a code rather than observing a value of a physical thing; there is no dimension and no measurement unit involved in issuing an accession number.

E15 Identifier Assignment is a sibling under E13 and is used elsewhere in this same model for the accession number, which makes the contrast sharp: the determination assigns a taxon, an E55 Type, to the specimen via P42, and treating a species name as an assigned identifier would lose that it is a classification carrying the classifier's judgement. Issue 77 settles the natural history reading in favour of E17.

notes:
Where I am less sure: the choice of S4 Single Observation over S21 Measurement / D11 Digital Measurement Event for the sequencing run. The argument is that a base-call sequence is not an E54 Dimension, but I could not fully check D11's declared path because its scope note references an observed-dimension property (O39) that returns "No such concept" - the CRMsci/CRMdig property coverage in the index is incomplete. Similarly connect S4 E20 did not offer O8 observed even though S15 Observable Entity subsumes E18 through S10, so I used O16 observed value and P140 assigned attribute to, which connect does confirm.

Tool problems worth reporting:

- concept P200 says "no definition in v7.1.3 (deprecated vocabulary)" and "CIDOC CRM v7.1.3 no longer defines this identifier", which reads as if P200 had been removed. In fact P200 has complete copy is a current property declared in the v7.3.2 reference document (chunk crm732#P200, domain E90, range E25) and is the resolution of issue 490. Because the concept/connect graph is built on the v7.1.3 XML, connect D9 E25 also does not offer it. Anyone relying on concept or connect alone would conclude a live property does not exist; I only found it through docs --kind declaration.

- connect needs its two class arguments as separate shell words. Passing them as a single quoted string does not error - it silently falls through to a mailing-list search and returns unrelated messages, identical for every pair. That cost me a full round of nine bogus results before I noticed.

- Extension classes (D*, S*, I*) print no Siblings block at all, so the rivals inside CRMsci, CRMdig and CRMinf had to be reconstructed by hand from the "Superclass of" lines of their parents (S27, D1, E13).

- CRMsci/CRMdig/CRMinf scope notes are not present in the docs corpus as addressable chunks, so quote cannot verify anything from them. Everything I took from S27, D9, D11, I6 and L61 is therefore paraphrased in my own words rather than quoted, even though I read it verbatim in concept output.

- Chunk ids are only visible with --json; the human-readable docs and issues output shows section paths but no ids, and quote will not accept "issue:77" or a bare issue number. Discovering the issue76#background-s0000 form required a --json round trip.
